messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

D-RUG will take place this Thursday from 12 - 2 pm. We will start with a mini-workshop on function writing with Reed. The second half of D-RUG will be open work time to make some progress on a project, ask questions, or hang out. As always, you can find us in person (360 Shields Library) or on zoom <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>.

Hope to see you there!
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

P.S. Check out our mini-workshop schedule for the quarter at the bottom of this email!

________________________________________________________________
Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

Mini-workshop schedule:
May 11: Iterations (for loops, map, apply functions)
May 18: Build a website with Rmarkdown and Github pages
May 25: R in the browser (WebR package)
June 1: Spatial data in R
June 8: Converting text into data with regular expressions

messages.subject: Fwd: Workshop announcement: A data analysis collaborator, June 20-30th, 2023.
messages.subject_clean: Workshop announcement: A data analysis collaborator, June 20-30th, 2023.
messages.body_plain:
Y’all would be most welcome! This will be _more_ command line and _less_ R specifically, but if it sparks your interest, I hope you consider joining us!

> Begin forwarded message:
>
> From: "C. Titus Brown" <ctb...@ucdavis.edu>
> Subject: Workshop announcement: A data analysis collaborator, June 20-30th, 2023.
> Date: May 11, 2023 at 7:20:17 AM PDT
> Reply-To: "ti...@idyll.org" <ti...@idyll.org>
>
> Please forward on - thank you!
> Workshop Annc: A data analysis collaboratory
>
> When: June 20th-30th, 2023, ~9am-5pm each day (except weekends; includes break for lunch).
> Where: Shields Library 360 (DataLab), UC Davis main campus.
> How much: Free
> Contact: Titus Brown, ctb...@ucdavis.edu
>
> This two week workshop will focus on improving the scalability and functionality of attendees’ existing data analysis research by using HPC and cloud best practices. The first week is a guided tour that will get everyone’s current Linux/R/Python-based workflows running on the UC Davis Farm compute cluster. The second week is a collaborative research computing hackyfest to level up those workflows by improving their speed, results, scalability, reproducibility, and validity. This in-person workshop at the UC Davis DataLab is open to all researchers, including graduate students. Researchers external to UCD are welcome as well!
>
> –
>
> Description
>
> This workshop is for researchers with already functioning data analysis projects who want to “level up” their project to take advantage of bigger resources (High Performance Computing and/or the cloud), use more automation, improve their reproducibility, expand their output formats and visualizations, conduct parameter sweeps, add more data sets, and/or otherwise work to improve and extend their current work.
>
> This is an interactive, hands-on workshop. Attendees should bring their own “pile of scripts,” workflows, large data sets, etc… This workshop is intended to help you make progress on your own research!
>
> The workshop is free and is only available for in-person participation. Space is limited. Any materials will be openly available after the workshop.
>
> The workshop will have a strong Code of Conduct.
>
> Recommended prerequisites. Prior to attending, learners should:
> be comfortable with the basics of remote computing & ssh (e.g., through Lesson 4 of this workshop series <https://ngs-docs.github.io/2021-august-remote-computing/>).
> have an already functioning project that makes use of R or Python scripts/notebooks or shell scripts on Linux or Mac OS X computers.
>
> Experience with any other specific technology is not required!
>
> Attendee information
> Attendees are expected to attend both weeks of this in person workshop. Events are scheduled from 9-5pm on weekdays, with no meetings on the weekends. There will be a flexibly scheduled break for lunch.
> The workshop will be held on UC Davis campus in the DataLab at Shields Library.
> UC Davis graduate students, postdocs, and faculty are welcome!
> External researchers are also welcome, space permitting!
> We cannot support work limited to closed or sensitive data sets as Farm is not HIPAA compliant; inquire for more information if you think this might pertain to you.
> We particularly welcome pairs of researchers from research groups who are working on related or overlapping projects!
>
> DataLab Affiliates will be given priority in case of space limitations.
>
> Workshop Content.
>
> Technologies that will be discussed and demonstrated during this workshop include, but are not limited to:
> shell scripting for automation
> conda for software installation
> slurm for HPC job coordination
> git and github for version control
> Python and JupyterLab
> R, RStudio, RMarkdown, Shiny (and maybe Posit)
> snakemake for workflow automation
> the Farm cluster for analysis (Other campus HPC will be supported on case by case basis; inquire for more information.)
>
> We are happy to work with any open source software that can be installed on remote Linux systems. Closed source or commercial software will be considered on a case by case basis.
>
> Concepts that will be discussed:
> designing computational workflows for enhanced science, better reproducibility, and improved efficiency
> parameter tuning and parameter sweeps
> integrating visualization and cross-validation into your workflows
> parallelism vs. I/O vs. memory intensive workflows
> getting your data ready for machine learning and AI
>
> –
> Apply by end of day on Wed, May 17th, 2023 for full consideration
>  <https://hackmd.io/ONG4bcrQSxi2kdR_ADTp2A?view#Application-link>
> Application link <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfmDxtOB7iY_icNP6NJ-WCTCoLNqWkJrKAakd4CpxFbHrywVQ/viewform>
>
> Apply here:
>
> Apply to the June 2023 data analysis collaboratory at UC Davis! <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfmDxtOB7iY_icNP6NJ-WCTCoLNqWkJrKAakd4CpxFbHrywVQ/viewform>
> docs.google.com <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfmDxtOB7iY_icNP6NJ-WCTCoLNqWkJrKAakd4CpxFbHrywVQ/viewform>
>
> We will confirm receipt of your application by May 17th and give you more information about the workshop then!
>  <https://hackmd.io/ONG4bcrQSxi2kdR_ADTp2A?view#Funding-and-support-acknowledgement>
> Funding and support acknowledgement
>
> This workshop is supported by internal funding to the UC Davis DataLab <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/>!

messages.subject: Part-time, short-term OpenStreetMap annotator job at Global Energy Monitor
messages.subject_clean: Part-time, short-term OpenStreetMap annotator job at Global Energy Monitor
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'd greatly appreciate it if you would consider applying (via direct email to me), or forwarding this to your networks and suggest folks get in touch with me directly. Thanks so much, in advance!

Ingrid

**************************

OpenStreetMap Annotator at Global Energy Monitor

Pay Type: Hourly
Starting Pay: $37.58/hour

Position Summary:

The OpenStreetMap Annotator will work collaboratively with Global Energy Monitor <https://globalenergymonitor.org/> and project partners. Through the web-based editing interface of OpenStreetMap (OSM) and other earth engines such as Bing and/or Google Earth, an OSM annotator will contribute to building a geolocated database of solar installations that can then be utilized for further analysis. The annotator will work closely with others supporting GEM's Global Solar Power Tracker <https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-solar-power-tracker/>.

This is a part-time, temporary, and remote position. The annotator will be able to work from home but must be based in the United States. This position will last between 3 and 6 months, and the annotator is expected to work at least 20 and no more than 29 hours per week.

Start date: July 3, 2023

Reports To:

Ingrid Behrsin -- Program Director, Renewables and Other Power
Responsibilities and Duties:

The position includes the following areas of responsibility.

Geolocate and appropriately label and annotate points and areas of interest in OpenStreetMap based on satellite imagery of solar installations.

Properly tag annotations by checking if such a tag exists or if a new one must be created.

Conduct web research and secondary literature analysis to determine and label attribute characteristics associated with solar installations in OSM.
Education and Experience:

1-2 years of experience annotating OpenStreetMap satellite imagery.

Knowledge/Skills:

Strong research skills, including attention to detail, scrupulous adherence to documented fact.

Resourcefulness in using online search tools, and triangulating online search results and secondary literature.

Basic knowledge of environmental and social impacts of energy production, governmental and business institutional structures, and the global political context of energy.

Demonstrated facility with computers, Global Information Systems (GIS) software, and Google Workplace apps.

Demonstrated ability to master additional technical skills as needed for data development and analysis.

Commitment to social and environmental justice.

--
